headline: Compare the outermost meaningful characters directly
statement: Return whether s reads the same forward and backward after ignoring non-alphanumeric characters and treating uppercase letters as lowercase. The normalized empty sequence is a palindrome.
intuition: Compare the first and last relevant characters, then move inward. Skip punctuation and spaces, and compare letters without case differences. A mismatch proves the string is not a palindrome. If all mirrored pairs match, the normalized text reads the same in both directions.
approach: Initialize left and right at the string ends.
Advance each pointer past non-alphanumeric characters.
Compare lowercase versions; a mismatch immediately returns false.
Move both pointers inward and return true when they meet or cross.
correctness: After skipping ignored characters, the two pointers select the first and last unmatched characters of the normalized sequence. Equal comparisons remove a valid mirrored pair. Any mismatch violates palindrome symmetry; exhausting all such pairs proves the sequence is palindromic.
bruteForce: Build a normalized string and compare it with its reverse: O(n) time and O(n) space.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n); additional space O(1). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Digits are alphanumeric and must be compared.
Do not compare punctuation before skipping it.
Pointer bounds matter for strings containing only punctuation.
